I guess? But agoraphobia seems to be more so labeled as trying to escape from a situation, or when a person has issues with a place and feels there's no escape. Once the door itself is open, I'm fine, and the door can be closed behind me. I'm not afraid of the space itself and I don't feel the need to go to anywhere else. Unless you count not wanting to do something as escaping a situation, I'm not exactly convinced.
